correctness.rationale: The reciprocal identity J[t,X]=t J[1/t,X] is exact, so it is enough to treat 0<t<=1. The hexagon's dihedral isometries reduce every unit pair to x=(1,a) on one edge and y on four canonical edge classes. For E0 and E3 one transformed norm is at most 1. For E1 the exact formulas A=max(1+tc,a+t) and B=1-ta+max(0,t-c) show that A>L and B>L would force simultaneously a>1/(1+t) and a<1/(1+t). For E2 the exact formulas A=-tb+max(1,a+t) and B=max(t+b,1+t-ta) give contradictions a>1 or a<1/(1+t) whenever both exceed L=(t^2+t+1)/(t+1). Reflection covers the remaining two edges. The explicit pair x=(1,0), y=(t/(1+t),1) has both transformed norms exactly L, proving sharpness.
risks: The all-parameter theorem rests on the analytic edge inequalities; the checker intentionally does not treat a finite grid as a proof of the continuum.
No classification of every maximizer is needed or claimed.

originality.rationale: The defining 2023 article was inspected through its affine-regular hexagon example, its skew von Neumann--Jordan example, and the full Section 5 defining J[t,X] and proving Propositions 5.1--5.3. It computes E[t,X] and C_NJ[X] on the hexagon but gives no J[t,X] value there. A later 2025/2026 generalized-mean paper was inspected because its family contains Fu's J[t,X] at mean exponent minus infinity. Its regular-hexagon examples are derived using an extreme-point reduction explicitly restricted to mean exponent t>=1, so their displayed positive-mean formula does not cover the minimum endpoint. published-finding corpus searches using exact notation, object aliases, formula aliases, and the source authors returned no covering statement. The current own ledger through generation g000056 contains no skew James J[t,X] hexagonal profile.
residual_risks: Bibliographic and semantic-index searches cannot establish absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The defining 2023 paper deliberately studies three related skew invariants and uses the affine-regular hexagon as a canonical non-Hilbert test object, but leaves its minimum-type J[t,X] profile uncomputed. The exact formula completes that canonical comparison rather than adding an arbitrary polygonal data point. It also exposes a structural limitation of Proposition 5.3: on the same standard example the general ordinary-James upper estimate has a strict, explicitly quantified gap for every unbalanced parameter. The result supplies a reusable piecewise-linear edge method for minimum-type skew invariants on polygonal norms.
risks: The result is a canonical exact benchmark and sharpness diagnosis, not a classification theorem for all polygonal spaces.
